newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria's president meets party leaders over poll.
newsitem.headline: Algeria's president meets party leaders over poll.

text.p: Algerian President Liamine Zeroual on Tuesday met 10 political party leaders to discuss preparations for parliamentary elections but the main secular opposition group stayed away, saying Algeria needs peace first.

Officials and party sources told Reuters by telephone from Algiers that an independent committee to supervise the elections planned for the first half of this year was the main topic on the meeting's agenda.
They said other items, including the worsening security situation, would be addressed because politicians were wary about possible low voter participation due to the continuing violence.

More than 60,000 people have died since Moslem guerrillas started attacks in 1992 after polls in which an Islamist party had taken a commanding lead were cancelled. During the holy fasting month of Ramadan that recently ended the guerrillas stepped up their attacks.

The main opposition party, Socialist Forces Front (FFS), dismissed Zeroual's invitation to take part in the talks saying such round the table meeting aimed only "to endorse decisions already taken by the authorities".

FFS has urged authorities since 1992 to open negotiations with the main opposition parties, including the outlawed Islamic Salvation Front -- which was banned after the polls were cancelled -- to end the bloodshed before holding elections.
